## Safety, ESD, privacy, and sealed PSU {.unnumbered}

Shut down and unplug before opening. Use the approved ESD area and handle parts by their edges. Never open or probe inside a PSU. Never photograph passwords, network secrets, private screens, or unnecessary serial numbers. Stop for liquid, a swollen cell, burnt areas, damaged power hardware, loose metal, sharp damage, smoke, unusual smell, abnormal heat, unstable power, or unexpected noise.

## Crossover procedure {.unnumbered}

Use identical USB models, the same USB-port type, the same waiting period, and the same test procedure where possible.

- **Round 1:** A runs Xubuntu live; B runs Mint Xfce live.
- **Round 2:** swap USB drives; A runs Mint Xfce live; B runs Xubuntu live.
- Live-USB boot time is **not** a fair computer-performance benchmark.

Record **Pass, Concern, or Fail** for each test. Green, Yellow, and Red are reserved for the final machine classification.

| Individual test | A Xubuntu | A Mint Xfce | B Xubuntu | B Mint Xfce |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| display | | | | |
| keyboard | | | | |
| mouse | | | | |
| cursor stability | | | | |
| USB | | | | |
| Ethernet | | | | |

## Authorization and acceptance {.unnumbered}

Do not erase, partition, install, replace storage, or move RAM without a signed teacher approval gate.

**Approved action and limits:** ______________________________________________________________________

**Teacher signature:** ____________________________________  **Date/time:** ____________________

After an approved installation: $\square$ restart/login  $\square$ display  $\square$ keyboard  $\square$ mouse/cursor  $\square$ USB  $\square$ Ethernet  $\square$ Wi-Fi  $\square$ sound  $\square$ storage  $\square$ updates

**Final classification:** A $\square$ Green $\square$ Yellow $\square$ Red  B $\square$ Green $\square$ Yellow $\square$ Red

Green means safe and stable. Yellow means one defined repair or closer review. Red means stop student work and isolate for teacher review.
